body:
The fallback `performance.now()` returns elapsed time since page load, not an absolute timestamp like `performance.timing.navigationStart`. This causes incorrect metric calculations when the fallback is used. Use `Date.now() - performance.now()` as the fallback to get an approximate navigation start timestamp.
```suggestion
    navigationStart:
      performance.timing?.navigationStart || Date.now() - performance.now(),
```

These metric calculations will produce incorrect or `NaN` results if `domContentLoaded` or `resourcesLoaded` are null (which can happen if the page loads very quickly before these events fire). Add null checks before calculation or set default values.
```suggestion
      'Navigation Start to DOM Ready':
        metrics.domContentLoaded != null
          ? (metrics.domContentLoaded - metrics.navigationStart).toFixed(2) + 'ms'
          : 'N/A',
      'Navigation Start to All Resources':
        metrics.resourcesLoaded != null
          ? (metrics.resourcesLoaded - metrics.navigationStart).toFixed(2) + 'ms'
          : 'N/A',
      'Time to Interactive': metrics.timeToInteractive.toFixed(2) + 'ms',
      'First Paint': metrics.firstPaint ? metrics.firstPaint.toFixed(2) + 'ms' : 'N/A',
      'First Contentful Paint': metrics.firstContentfulPaint
        ? metrics.firstContentfulPaint.toFixed(2) + 'ms'
        : 'N/A',

This breaks the progress bar animation entirely since `state.progressElement` remains `null` and is never reassigned.

### `state.isReady` is never set to true **Medium Severity** The `state.isReady` property is initialized to `false` but never updated to `true` anywhere in the code. The public API `window.AffineDriftStartup.isReady()` will always return `false`, even after the page is fully loaded and the splash screen has been hidden.
Additional Locations (1) - [`js/startup-launcher.js#L434-L435`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/AffineDrift/blob/a036cf6719a232c938efc51966db971bc3b1f41d/js/startup-launcher.js#L434-L435)

### Status text can regress to earlier loading stage **Low Severity** The `updateProgress` function always updates the status text even when the progress target doesn't increase (due to `Math.max`). If fonts (60%) load after resources (80%), the status will regress from 'Finalizing...' back to 'Loading fonts...' while progress stays at 80%, creating a confusing user experience.

### Metrics use incompatible timestamp formats causing wrong values **Medium Severity** `metrics.navigationStart` uses `performance.timing?.navigationStart` which is an absolute timestamp (milliseconds since Unix epoch, ~1.7 trillion), but later metrics like `domContentLoaded`, `resourcesLoaded`, and `splashHidden` use `performance.now()` which returns relative milliseconds since time origin (~500).
